items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Dick was interviewed by Monk Rowe on March 4, 1995 in Scottsdale, Arizona.

ctx.x: Highlights in his recording career include “The Complete Works of Scott Joplin,” “Seven Ages of Jazz,” numerous trio albums and one of the first synthesizer-based recordings. His arrangements have found a home with Count Basie, Doc Severinsen, The Mills Brothers and Al Hirt, and he is well known for his film scoring for Woody Allen. Born in New York City on March 3, 1927, he eventually found himself playing behind some of the greatest jazz stars, including Charlie Parker, Lester Young and Benny Goodman.…
Dick was interviewed by Monk Rowe on March 4, 1995 in Scottsdale, Arizona.

We are here today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive and we have the great pleasure of talking with Mr. Dick Hyman, who has been described in a number of ways: eclectic, versatile, a Renaissance Man, and, I want to see if we can figure out when all that started and perhaps we’ll discuss why he’s called all those things.
